evidence: Constructive proof by an explicit (τ+1)×(τ+1) minor with unit determinant and a row-span upper bound; no finite computation is needed.
proved_step:
statement: For every field F and integer τ≥0, the infinite Hankel matrix H=(a_{i+j})_{i,j≥0} of the sequence a_t=[t≥τ] has rank exactly τ+1 over F.
proof: For 0≤i,j≤τ, consider the square submatrix B with B_ij=[i+j≥τ]. Reverse its columns. In the resulting matrix, entry (i,k) is 1 exactly when i≥k, so it is lower triangular with every diagonal entry 1. Its determinant is 1, hence B has rank τ+1 over every field. For the upper bound, every row with index i≥τ is the all-ones row. The first τ+1 rows span all rows: indeed, the rows indexed 0 through τ are independent by the same square minor, and every row is among these rows or is the all-ones row, which is row τ. Therefore the row space has dimension at most τ+1. Together the bounds give rank τ+1.

statement: Let F be any field, let tau>=1, and let (a_t) be a sequence with a_t=c for every t>=tau, where c is nonzero and a_{tau-1} != c. Then the infinite Hankel matrix H=(a_{i+j})_{i,j>=0} has rank exactly tau+1 over F.
proof: Every row with index i>=tau is the constant row (c,c,...), so the row space is spanned by rows 0,...,tau and rank is at most tau+1. For the reverse bound, take the leading (tau+1)-square Hankel minor B=(a_{i+j})_{0<=i,j<=tau}. Reverse its columns to obtain C_{ij}=a_{tau+i-j}. For i>=j this entry is c, and for i<j it is an arbitrary prefix term. Subtract row i-1 from row i, in descending order i=tau,...,1. Each resulting row i has zero entries in columns j<i and has entry c-a_{tau-1} in column i; entries in columns j>i may be arbitrary. The first row has entry c in column 0. Thus the resulting matrix is upper triangular with diagonal c,c-a_{tau-1},...,c-a_{tau-1}, so det(B)=det(C)=c*(c-a_{tau-1})^tau !=0. Hence rank is at least tau+1, proving equality.

refuted_approach: S0002 determinant identity omitted the sign from reversing the tau+1 columns. Counterexample: tau=1, F3, prefix a0=0, c=1 gives determinant -1 rather than +1. The nonzero-determinant and rank conclusion survive after correcting the sign.
proved_step:
statement: Let F be any field, tau>=1, and a sequence (a_t) satisfy a_t=c for every t>=tau, where c!=0 and a_{tau-1}!=c. Its infinite Hankel matrix H=(a_{i+j})_{i,j>=0} has rank exactly tau+1 over F. More precisely, the leading minor B=(a_{i+j})_{0<=i,j<=tau} has determinant (-1)^(tau*(tau+1)/2) c (c-a_{tau-1})^tau.
proof: Reverse the columns of B to form C, where C_ij=a_{tau+i-j}. For i>=j, C_ij=c. Perform row operations in descending order i=tau,...,1, replacing row i by row i minus row i-1. Descending order preserves each row i-1 in its original form when used. In the resulting matrix, row 0 has entry c in column 0. For row i>=1 and column j<i, both C_ij and C_(i-1),j equal c, so the difference is zero. At column j=i, C_i,i=c and C_(i-1),i=a_(tau-1), so the difference is c-a_(tau-1). Thus the transformed matrix is upper triangular with diagonal c followed by tau copies of c-a_(tau-1). Its determinant is c(c-a_(tau-1))^tau. Reversing tau+1 columns has sign (-1)^(tau*(tau+1)/2), so det(B)=(-1)^(tau*(tau+1)/2)c(c-a_(tau-1))^tau, which is nonzero. Hence rank(H)>=tau+1. Every row i>=tau of H is the constant row (c,c,...), equal to row tau; thus all rows lie in the span of rows 0,...,tau and rank(H)<=tau+1. Equality follows.

statement: Let F be a field and let x=(x_t) and y=(y_t), t>=0, have infinite Hankel matrices H_x=(x_{i+j}) and H_y=(y_{i+j}) of finite ranks r and s. Define z_t=x_t y_t. Then rank(H_z)<=rs.
proof: By finite rank, each Hankel matrix admits a rank-factorization: x_{i+j}=sum_{a=1}^r u_a(i)v_a(j) and y_{i+j}=sum_{b=1}^s p_b(i)q_b(j). (Equivalently, factor every finite submatrix consistently through the finite-dimensional row and column spaces.) Thus z_{i+j}=x_{i+j}y_{i+j}=sum_{a=1}^r sum_{b=1}^s [u_a(i)p_b(i)][v_b(j)q_b(j)], a sum of rs separated row-column terms. Every finite submatrix of H_z therefore has rank at most rs, so the infinite matrix has rank at most rs.
